prompts.display_text: Pin a country where a new temple was dedicated from 2010 to 2015 (not rededications).
prompts.text_original: A country where a new temple was dedicated from 2010 through 2015 (not counting rededications).
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org chronological list (original dedication dates) and the Church temple list, read 26 Oct 2026
prompts.summary: From 2010 to 2015 first temples were dedicated in Ukraine (Kyiv, 2010), El Salvador (San Salvador, 2011) and Honduras (Tegucigalpa, 2013). Other new temples included Cebu City Philippines, Vancouver and Calgary in Canada, Manaus Brazil, and Tijuana Mexico, Córdoba Argentina and Trujillo Peru in 2015.

prompts.display_text: Pin a Latin American country with a temple standing today that Gordon B. Hinckley dedicated or rededicated.
prompts.text_original: Pin a Latin American country where Gordon B. Hinckley dedicated or rededicated a temple now in use (as of October 2026).
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org chronological list (dedicated-by column), read 26 Oct 2026
prompts.summary: Gordon B. Hinckley dedicated temples throughout Latin America. He dedicated Mexico City and Santiago Chile in 1983, Guatemala City in 1984 and Lima Peru in 1986. Later came Bogotá and Guayaquil (1999), Cochabamba, Caracas, Santo Domingo, Recife and Porto Alegre (2000), Montevideo (2001) and Asunción (2002).

prompts.display_text: Pin a present-day country on the Red Sea, whose shore Lehi's family followed (1 Nephi 2:5).
prompts.text_original: Lehi's family traveled 'by the borders near the shore of the Red Sea' (1 Nephi 2:5). Pin a country on the Red Sea
prompts.note: Places in the West Bank or Gaza, such as Bethlehem, Hebron, Jericho or Gaza city, count as Palestine, which is not an answer.
prompts.summary: Warned in a dream that people sought his life, Lehi left his home and lands with his family about 600 BC and traveled near the shore of the Red Sea (1 Nephi 2:1-5). After three days they camped in a valley by a river he named Laman, which emptied into the Red Sea (1 Nephi 2:6-8).

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Egypt's eastern coast lies on the Red Sea and the Gulf of Suez.

answers.name: Saudi Arabia
answers.fact: Has a long Red Sea coast on the Arabian side.

answers.name: Sudan
answers.fact: Has a Red Sea coast around Port Sudan.

answers.name: Yemen
answers.fact: Holds the southern Arabian shore of the Red Sea down to the Bab-el-Mandeb strait.

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Touches the Red Sea at Eilat on the Gulf of Aqaba.

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: Touches the Red Sea at Aqaba on the Gulf of Aqaba.

answers.name: Djibouti
answers.fact: Sits at the Red Sea's southern mouth, the Bab-el-Mandeb.

answers.name: Eritrea
answers.fact: Has an extensive Red Sea coastline, including the Dahlak Archipelago.

prompts.display_text: Pin a Pacific country or territory whose Indigenous language has Book of Mormon text.
prompts.text_original: A Pacific country or territory whose Indigenous language has a Book of Mormon translation or selections
prompts.summary: The Book of Mormon has a long history in Pacific languages. Hawaiian came first, in 1855, translated by George Q. Cannon, followed by Maori (1889), Samoan (1903), Tahitian (1904) and Tongan (1946). Later translations reached Fiji, Kiribati, the Marshall Islands, Micronesia and other islands.

answers.name: New Zealand
answers.fact: Maori got the Book of Mormon in 1889.

answers.name: Tonga
answers.fact: Tongan got the Book of Mormon in 1946.

answers.name: Samoa
answers.fact: Samoan got the Book of Mormon in 1903.

answers.name: Fiji
answers.fact: Fijian got the Book of Mormon in 1980.

answers.name: French Polynesia
answers.fact: Tahitian got the Book of Mormon in 1904.

answers.name: United States
answers.fact: Hawaiian, translated by George Q. Cannon, appeared in 1855.

answers.name: American Samoa
answers.fact: Samoan, translated 1903, is the territory's own language.

answers.name: Cook Islands
answers.fact: Rarotongan got the Book of Mormon in 1965.

answers.name: Micronesia
answers.fact: Pohnpeian, Chuukese, Yapese and Kosraean all have Book of Mormon text.

answers.name: Kiribati
answers.fact: Kiribati selections came in 1988 and the full text in 2001.

answers.name: Marshall Islands
answers.fact: Marshallese selections came in 1984 and the full text in 2003.

answers.name: Guam
answers.fact: Chamorro selections appeared in 1989.

answers.name: Northern Mariana Islands
answers.fact: Chamorro, given selections in 1989, is Indigenous here too.

answers.name: Niue
answers.fact: Niuean selections appeared in 1981.

answers.name: Palau
answers.fact: Palauan selections appeared in 1988.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country with a Bible city that is or was a nation's or kingdom's capital (not Jerusalem).
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a city named in the Bible that is or was the capital of a nation or kingdom (not Jerusalem)
prompts.citation: Genesis 14; Joshua 11; 1 Samuel 27; 2 Samuel 12; 1 Kings 5; 2 Kings 16; Esther; Jonah; Jeremiah 46; Acts 17; Romans 1
prompts.note: Places in the West Bank or Gaza, such as Bethlehem, Hebron, Jericho or Gaza city, count as Palestine, which is not an answer.
prompts.summary: Many Bible stories take place in royal cities. Nineveh and Babylon were capitals in today's Iraq, Shushan in Iran was a Persian royal seat in the book of Esther, and Damascus was the capital of Aram and is the capital of Syria today. Tyre was the seat of King Hiram, who supplied cedar for Solomon's temple, and Rabbah of the Ammonites is modern Amman in Jordan.

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: Nineveh of Assyria and Babylon were both capitals in Iraq.

answers.name: Italy
answers.fact: Rome is the destination of Acts and of Paul's letter.

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Noph (Memphis) and No (Thebes) were Egyptian capitals (Jeremiah 46).

answers.name: Greece
answers.fact: Paul preached at the Areopagus in Athens (Acts 17).

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: Damascus, capital of Aram and of Syria today, appears from Genesis to Acts.

answers.name: Iran
answers.fact: Shushan (Susa) was a Persian royal seat in Esther.

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Hazor was the head of the northern kingdoms (Joshua 11:10), Achish was king of Gath (1 Samuel 27:2), and Ashdod was a Philistine seat.

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: Tyre was the seat of King Hiram (1 Kings 5).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: Rabbah of the Ammonites is modern Amman (2 Samuel 12:26).
